title: Pinning Fallbacks, Region Affinity and Routing Compatibility Matrix
content:
Purpose:
This note captures operational patterns and a proposed scoring matrix for how model registry version pinning should interact with routing decisions across regions, capacity tiers and compatibility constraints. It focuses on safe fallback behaviors and a compact compatibility scoring rubric that the control plane can evaluate at request-time.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to hosted + dedicated + private control-plane modes where central registry metadata informs routing.
- We assume model artifacts declare: semantic_version, family (e.g., llama-70b), quantization_profile, and a compatibility hint list (backward/forward flags).
- Goal is to avoid silent behavior regressions while providing low-latency fallbacks.

Problem statement:
When a customer pins to model X:vA, requests must prefer vA but remain resilient if capacity/region constraints require fallback. Current debates: whether to allow auto-fallback to older or newer minor versions, to different quantization variants, or to model-family-compatible substitutes. We need an auditable, score-driven decision that is deterministic and explainable.

Design principles:
- Safety-first: avoid silent quality regressions. Any fallback that may change response semantics must be surfaced in logs and optionally in response metadata.
- Locality: prefer region-local fallbacks to minimize latency/egress costs.
- Compatibility scoring: compute a single numeric score per candidate for deterministic selection.
- Operator controls: admins can set strictness policies per org (e.g., require exact-match, allow minor upgrades only, allow quantization flips).

Compatibility scoring rubric (illustrative):
Each candidate model M' yields a score S = W_version*V + W_quant*Q + W_region*R + W_capacity*C + W_policy*P (0..100). Higher is better.
- V (version closeness): exact pin => 100, same minor semver => 80, same major => 50, different family => 0.
- Q (quantization delta): identical quant profile => 100, lower precision => 50 (flagged), higher precision => 90.
- R (region affinity): same AZ => 100, same region diff AZ => 90, cross-region same continent => 70, cross-continent => 40.
- C (capacity headroom): healthy pool (>=40% headroom) => 100, burstable (<40% but available) => 60, constrained => 20.
- P (policy multiplier): if customer policy forbids change => 0, if customer allows only non-regressive upgrades => 100, else 80.
Weights defaults: W_version=0.4, W_quant=0.2, W_region=0.15, W_capacity=0.15, W_policy=0.1. Tunable by org.

Routing decision flow (simplified):
1) Gather candidate models in registry that claim compatibility with request-model-family.
2) Filter by policy hard constraints (policy P hard zeros eliminate candidates).
3) Compute S for each remaining candidate; if top S >= threshold T_accept (default 60) select candidate.
4) If multiple candidates within 5 points, apply tiebreaker: prefer higher V then R then C.
5) If no candidate meets threshold, failover to configured safety mode: retry after 200ms to same region, then attempt cross-region acceptable models, then return error if all fail.

Example routing compatibility matrix (human-readable snapshot):
Columns: CandidateVersion | semver relation | quant delta | region dist | capacity | computed S | accept? | notes
- v2.1.0 | exact pin | q4f32 | same-AZ | healthy | 100 | yes | ideal
- v2.1.1 | minor bump | q4f32 | same-region-diff-AZ | healthy | 88 | yes | allowed (minor upgrade)
- v2.0.5 | older minor | q4q8 | same-region | burstable | 62 | yes | quant change flagged
- v3.0.0 | major upgrade | q4f32 | cross-continent | healthy | 45 | no | semantics may differ
- familyX-2.3 | different family | q4f32 | same-region | healthy | 20 | no | incompatible family

Operational safeguards and observability:
- Telemetry: every routed request logs chosen candidate id, S breakdown vector, registry-revision used, policy-id and region.
- Alerts: raise if >0.5% of pinned requests are served by non-pinned models for >10m window unless explicitly allowed.
- Explainability: API response header X-Model-Routing: {chosen:id, reason:score, fallback_category} when non-pinned model used. Optional verbose wire format for paid tiers.
- Audit: keep immutable routing-decision events for 30 days in hosted. Private installs opt-in.

Compatibility test matrix (CI plan):
- Unit tests: scoring math, edge-case zeros, tiebreakers.
- Integration: simulate capacity loss in a region, ensure pinned clients are rescheduled using expected candidate order.
- Chaos tests: random AZ/network partitions, verify fallback thresholds and alerting behave.
- Eval-run: run canonical prompt set for pin v2.1.0 and compare outputs if fallback chosen — compute quality delta; if delta > configured regression_threshold, escalate.

Example policy presets (admin controls):
- strict: allow only exact semver matches; any mismatch => error.
- safe-upgrade: allow patch/minor upgrades with equal-or-better quant; deny older models.
- cost-aware: allow quantized older models if cost benefits and score >= threshold.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should we expose the full score vector to customers? (privacy & gaming concerns)
- How to handle function-calling / tool-calling model semantic changes across major versions? Conservative approach: major-version mismatch must be manually approved.
- How to represent model family semantics beyond semver (behavioral tags)? e.g., hallucination profile, safety level.

Implementation notes / quick tasks:
- Registry: add fields compatibility_hints (list), min_acceptable_major, behavioral_tags.
- Control plane: implement scoring module in router service, caching of candidate scores with short TTL (5s) to avoid recompute storms.
- Console: expose per-org policy UI and per-version compatibility visualization.

Next steps:
- Sync with applied-ml on behavioral tags semantics (owner: Marta, 2 weeks).
- Build prototype scoring service and run chaos-sim for US-1 region (owner: Evan, 3 weeks).
- Draft admin UX for policy presets (owner: Kenji, 4 weeks).

Notes to reviewers:
This is intentionally pragmatic (score+threshold) rather than math-perfect. The goal is an operationally simple, auditable heuristic that prevents silent quality regressions while enabling reasonable fallbacks. Feedback: please call out missing failure modes or policy permutations you hit in production.
